title: Oatmeal, regular or quick, made with water

content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal consists of whole or rolled oat grains prepared with water and no added fat. It is available in regular and quick‑cooking forms, absorbs water rapidly, and forms a thick porridge rich in complex carbohydrates and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown by humans for over 5,000 years.
Quick‑cooking oatmeal is steamed and cut into thin flakes, reducing cooking time to 1–3 minutes.
Oat flakes contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol levels.
Oats are frequently used in cosmetics for their soothing and moisturizing properties.
Traditional medicine uses oats to aid digestion and regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Rich in complex carbs
items.content: Oatmeal provides sustained energy and prolonged satiety due to the slow release of glucose.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucan
items.content: This soluble fiber helps reduce LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and supports heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Oats supply thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Oatmeal is a good source of magnesium, iron, zinc, and phosphorus, supporting muscles, bones, and immunity.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in oats promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can impair mineral absorption; soaking oats before cooking can reduce this effect.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same equipment as wheat, so people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free oats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook oatmeal in water, adding a pinch of salt. Sweeten with honey, fruit, berries, nuts, or spices such as cinnamon or vanilla. Quick oatmeal is ready in 1–3 minutes; regular oatmeal takes 5–10 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oat flakes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth.
